answer: Submission rate is limited to 10 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole farm from one uplink. An operator running many aliases as a result pays for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the zephyr quota and the hollow admission check. Because the counters live in the ember ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
